purpose: Test the proposed known-partner rank-one complement-noise family's erasure cost before any amplitude search. Not an unknown-partner defense or an innovation claim.
construction: Centered real target/partner training moments on the target expert. Restrict to the target PCA complement excluding LayerNorm's exact affine null direction. Maximize partner top-subspace overlap; use the partner task increment's leading left singular vector. Generate one representative rank-one edit per fixed site only for algebra checks, not utility certification or candidate selection.
recovery: Replace the complete edited input projection and bias with public pretrained values. For V only the value slice is replaced; Q/K, output projection, LayerNorm and all other fields stay unchanged. This erases every additive perturbation confined to that support, independently of rank, amplitude, output direction, calibration or partner alignment.
evaluation: Nine fresh full evaluations: original target standalone plus two-task TA(.5) on target and partner; the same three measurements for each public reset. No test-based construction or selection, no AGA/TIES/DARE/query expansion if the cheap recovery gate fails. Raw predictions and representative edits stay on server.
limitations: Previously observed official tests and historical training calibration, not new holdout. Partner checkpoint and inputs are used, violating unknown-future-partner protection scope. PCA complement is not an exact task nullspace. No standalone utility or fusion-security claim for representative edits. Conclusions are restricted to each stated single-projection support and this fusion protocol.
